title: docmeta eval declarations (1.0.0-proposal.1)
description: Page-level eval declarations: named, testable assertions about a page, each graded by code, an AI judge (a model or an agent), or a human. A docmeta common vocabulary: any grader, judge, or CI tool can implement it, and other schemas may compose on top of it. It adopts the house conventions — kebab-case keys, flat page-level facts — and claims four keys: `evals` (one assertion or the list), `eval-suite`, `eval-skip`, and `eval-provenance`. There is no settings container: settings are page-level facts, and generation attribution lives at the page's top-level `generated-by` (docmeta:ai-context:1.0.0-proposal.1). Because the page root is open, consumers should reserve the `eval-` prefix and reject unrecognized `eval-*` keys, giving the root the loud-typo property a closed container would have.

evals.description: The evals for this page: one AI-judged assertion as a string, or a non-empty list of entries — each a string shorthand, a `use:` reference to a config-defined eval, or an inline definition. An empty list is not a declaration; a page with no evals omits the key.

eval-suite.description: Named suite from the config whose evals apply to this page, alongside anything in `evals`. Page entries win on id collision. A suite assignment is a page-level fact.

eval-skip.description: Skip this page's evals entirely — reported as skipped, never silently ignored. Default false.

eval-provenance.description: Attribution for machine-proposed evals, one entry per model (consumers merge by generated-by; the schema dedupes identical entries): which eval ids it proposed, at what confidence. A human deletes an entry once those evals are reviewed. The same pattern as page-level `provenance` and kg's, under the reserved `eval-` prefix consumers already police.

generated-by.description: Model or agent that proposed the evals.

confidence.description: Per-eval model confidence, 0..1, keyed by the same kebab eval ids as `evals` — a confidence attached to a malformed id fails here instead of dangling.

else.description: An object entry: a `use:` reference to a config-defined eval, else an inline definition. Branched with if/then rather than oneOf so a fault inside the object form is reported once, against the key that is wrong — the same rule the starlight built-in records.

evalEntry.description: One eval: a string shorthand (an AI-judged assertion at error severity), or an object.

use.description: Name of an eval defined in the config.

id.description: Unique (per page) kebab-case identifier for this eval. `id` matches the page-level `id` convention — in this family, `name` would mean a display name.

assertion.description: The testable assertion, in plain language.

provider.description: Which configured inference provider or agent judges an `ai`-graded eval — a model endpoint or an agent runner. Legal values are whatever the inference dependency supports, validated at run time; omit for the config default. Meaningful only on `ai` evals.

evidence.description: Hint scoping where the judge should look for evidence.

examples.description: Anchor examples of passing and failing content for the judge — one or several each.

command.description: Command to execute for command-graded evals. {file} is replaced with the page path, and exit 0 (or `success-exit-codes`) is a pass. Omitting it is the generation contract: tooling generates a check script from the assertion, then writes `command` and `generated-assertion-hash` back. Legal only alongside `grader: command`.

success-exit-codes.description: Exit codes that count as a pass.

timeout-ms.description: Wall-clock budget for the command, in milliseconds.

generated-assertion-hash.description: sha256 of the assertion when the check script was generated — written back alongside `command`, and never legal without it: a hash with no command is a half write-back, and a command with a differing hash triggers regeneration.

options.description: Grader-specific options; validated by the grader at run time.

severity-map.description: Maps a tool grader's own severities onto eval severities. Meaningful only on `tool:*` evals.

then.description: An entry carrying an executable command must say grader: command — an execution payload on an ai or human eval is either dead weight or a surprise, depending on which field the runner keys on.

success-exit-codes and timeout-ms configure command execution, so they are legal only alongside grader: command — with or without the command itself, since the generation contract writes the command later. On an ai or human eval they are dead weight the runner never reads.

evalType.description: `capability` probes a boundary and is expected to fail sometimes; `regression` protects behavior that already works.

severity.description: Only error-severity failures fail the run; warning and info report but pass. Default error — the string shorthand implies it.

grader.description: How the assertion is checked: an AI judge (`ai`) — a direct inference provider or an agent, selected per-eval with `provider`; an executable check (`command`), generated from the assertion when no `command` is given; a human review queue (`human`); or a named tool integration (`tool:<kebab>`) — an open family, extensible without touching this schema. The judge may be an agent rather than a bare model — hence `ai`, not `llm`. The structural kinds stay closed because the conditionals above switch on them.

anchorList.description: One anchor example, or a non-empty list of them.
